title: MindUnitScores
description: An editor's markup of every sentence in a recording: which lines would open a clip well, which lines land a thought, which ranges a tight cut can leave out (a tangent, a retake, a false start, filler, an aside, an ad read) and which sentences cannot stand without an earlier one. The model marks only what stands out, a window of the annotated script at a time, citing sentences it was shown; code writes the row for every sentence, so a sentence with nothing marked is an ordinary line, not a missing one. Windows the model could not mark are listed under `unscored`. This is what lets the cutter tighten a moment and start a clip on its strongest line.

units.description: One row per sentence, in recording order.

hook.description: How well the line would open a clip for someone who has heard nothing before it, from `none` to `strong`: a line people stop scrolling for.

landing.description: How well the line ends a thought, from `none` (it leaves things hanging) to `strong` (a clean conclusion, punchline or turn).

trim.description: `keep`, or why a tight cut may leave the line out.

needs.description: An earlier sentence this one cannot be understood without: the thing a pronoun points at, the question it answers.
